chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked him (peace be upon him) while I was in his presence, regarding a man who struck another man and his urine stream was interrupted. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the urine trickles into the night, upon him is the complete wergild (diyah), because it has prevented him from his livelihood; and if it is into the end of the day, upon him is the complete wergild; and if it is into half the day, upon him is two-thirds of the wergild; and if it is into the raising of the day, upon him is one-third of the wergild.'

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Wergild or blood money, financial compensation for injury or death

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on compensation for injury to the urinary tract?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a precise, time-based methodology for calculating 'diyah' (blood money) for urinary tract injuries, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of linking compensation to the actual loss of livelihood or function. The Imam (peace be upon him) differentiates between full and partial impairment based on whether the condition persists through the night or specific portions of the day, demonstrating a nuanced approach to bodily damages that balances legal certainty with equitable restitution.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘A man asked him<sup>asws</sup> and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, ‘A man struck a man, so his urine was intermittent. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was that the urine trickled into the night, so upon him is the (complete) wergild, because it has prevented him from the livelihood; and if it was into the end of the day, so upon him is the (complete) wergild; and if it was into half the day, so upon him is a third of the wergild; and if it was into the raising of the day, so upon his is a third of the wergild’.
